_comment: Copy this to the audited repo and delete the underscore keys. Preferred location
is .tld/test-audit-baseline.json; if the repo gitignores .tld/, use
.claude/test-audit-baseline.json or test-audit-baseline.json at the root, so the
file is committed and reviewed like any other code.
Nothing in this file may be time-bound. No month, no year, no run counts, no
'as of' notes. It is read unattended for years, and a stale constant does not
raise an error, it just quietly stops matching.
Every regex is a JavaScript regex in a JSON string, so each backslash is doubled.

_comment_runners: One entry per test runner configuration in the repo, and the audit is only as
honest as this list. A test file no declared runner collects is reported as
suite-not-collected, so a runner you forget to declare turns its whole suite
into false findings, and a runner that genuinely does not exist hides real
ones. include_regex matches the repo-relative POSIX path.
Leave the list empty and the collection check reports SKIPPED, never a pass.
_comment_ci: Where CI job definitions live, and which job names own tests. A job whose name
matches ci_test_job_regex and whose condition is constantly false is reported:
it reports as satisfied on every run without executing anything.
Leave ci_workflow_dir empty and that check reports SKIPPED, never a pass.
_comment_tracker: Only needed when the repo has no .tld/campaign.md. That file always wins.
ticket_labels are the STABLE labels every filed ticket carries and the de-dup
search looks for. Never put a dated label here. The skill adds a dated grouping
label at filing time, built from the real date of the run.
_comment_patterns: Every pattern below has a working default in the engine and only needs setting
when this project genuinely differs. Loosen one and the check goes quiet, which
is the failure this whole file exists to prevent, so change them deliberately.
assertion_helper_regex is the usual one worth setting: it teaches the engine
that a call like expectRowCount(...) is an assertion. Helpers defined in the
same file are detected automatically and need no entry here.

_comment_accepted: Reviewed exceptions. A row here is suppressed entirely and counted, so adding a
name is a sign-off: you opened the file, read the case, and concluded the check
is over-flagging on a pattern that is genuinely fine. It is never a way to quiet
a noisy check. Every entry carries a reason written for someone who was not
there, saying what was checked and what made it benign. A reason that only says
'known' or 'by design' is not a reason.
Omit check to accept an object for every check.

accepted.reason: Runner project scoping, not a disabled test. The skip reads test.skip(testInfo.project.name !== 'chromium', ...) and playwright.config.ts defines a chromium project, so the condition is false there and the case executes.

_comment_known_open: Findings that are real and already on a ticket. They report as KNOWN-OPEN <key>
instead of NEW, so a recurring sweep stops re-filing them, and they are never
Prune a row when its ticket closes. A closed ticket left in this list suppresses
the finding forever, which is the one way this check goes quiet while the defect
is still in the tree. The skill re-checks the status of every key it reads.
